audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph census, plague, angel, and Ornan threshing-floor narrative, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed against 2 Samuel 24 for Satan/YHWH agency contradiction, census purpose and numbers, Joab's refusal, collective punishment, famine/war/plague choice, seventy-thousand deaths, stopping command, David's responsibility, sheep metaphor, Ornan and sons, coerced land transaction, price variants, altar fire, and David's fear.

verses.restored: An adversary/Satan stood against Israel and incited David to count Israel.

familiar.text: And Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to number Israel.

modern.text: Then Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to take a census of Israel.

original.text: וַיַּֽעֲמֹ֥ד שָׂטָ֖ן עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֨סֶת֙ אֶת דָּוִ֔יד לִמְנ֖וֹת אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: David said to Joab and rulers of people, Go, count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring number to me so I may know it.

familiar.text: And David said to Joab and to the rulers of the people, Go, number Israel from Beersheba even to Dan; and bring the number of them to me, that I may know it.

modern.text: So David said to Joab and the commanders of the troops, “Go and count the Israelites from Beersheba to Dan and bring me a report, so that I may know their number.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤יד אֶל יוֹאָב֙ וְאֶל שָׂרֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם לְכ֗וּ סִפְרוּ֙ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִבְּאֵ֥ר שֶׁ֖בַע וְעַד דָּ֑ן וְהָבִ֣יאוּ אֵלַ֔י וְאֵדְעָ֖ה אֶת מִסְפָּרָֽם

verses.restored: Joab said, May YHWH add to people a hundred times. My lord king, are they not all servants of my lord? Why does my lord seek this? Why should it become guilt for Israel?

familiar.text: And Joab answered, The LORD make his people an hundred times so many more as they be: but, my lord the king, are they not all my lord’s servants? why then doth my lord require this thing? why will he be a cause of trespass to Israel?

modern.text: But Joab replied, “May the LORD multiply His troops a hundred times over. My lord the king, are they not all servants of my lord? Why does my lord want to do this? Why should he bring guilt on Israel?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֗ב יוֹסֵף֩ יְהוָ֨ה עַל עַמּ֤וֹ כָּהֵם֙ מֵאָ֣ה פְעָמִ֔ים הֲלֹא֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כֻּלָּ֥ם לַאדֹנִ֖י לַעֲבָדִ֑ים לָ֣מָּה יְבַקֵּ֥שׁ זֹאת֙ אֲדֹנִ֔י לָ֛מָּה יִהְיֶ֥ה לְאַשְׁמָ֖ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: King's word prevailed over Joab. Joab went throughout all Israel and came to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Nevertheless the king’s word prevailed against Joab. Wherefore Joab departed, and went throughout all Israel, and came to Jerusalem.

modern.text: Nevertheless, the king’s word prevailed against Joab. So Joab departed and traveled throughout Israel, and then he returned to Jerusalem.

original.text: וּדְבַר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חָזַ֣ק עַל יוֹאָ֑ב וַיֵּצֵ֣א יוֹאָ֗ב וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ֙ בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיָּבֹ֖א יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: Joab gave total count to David: all Israel, one million one hundred thousand sword-drawing men; Judah, four hundred seventy thousand sword-drawing men.

familiar.text: And Joab gave the sum of the number of the people unto David. And all they of Israel were a thousand thousand and an hundred thousand men that drew sword: and Judah was four hundred threescore and ten thousand men that drew sword.

modern.text: And Joab reported to David the total number of the troops. In all Israel there were 1,100,000 men who drew the sword, including 470,000 in Judah.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת מִסְפַּ֥ר מִפְקַד הָעָ֖ם אֶל דָּוִ֑יד וַיְהִ֣י כָֽל יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל אֶ֣לֶף אֲלָפִים֩ וּמֵאָ֨ה אֶ֤לֶף אִישׁ֙ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֔רֶב וִֽיהוּדָ֕ה אַרְבַּע֩ מֵא֨וֹת וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ שֹׁ֥לֵֽף חָֽרֶב

verses.restored: Levi and Benjamin he did not count among them, for king's word was abhorrent to Joab.

familiar.text: But Levi and Benjamin counted he not among them: for the king’s word was abominable to Joab.

modern.text: But Joab did not include Levi and Benjamin in the count, because the king’s command was detestable to him. Judgment for David’s Sin (2 Samuel 24:10–14)

original.text: וְלֵוִי֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן לֹ֥א פָקַ֖ד בְּתוֹכָ֑ם כִּֽי נִתְעַ֥ב דְּבַר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת יוֹאָֽב

verses.restored: This matter was evil in eyes of Divine, and Divine struck Israel.

familiar.text: And God was displeased with this thing; therefore he smote Israel.

modern.text: This command was also evil in the sight of God; so He struck Israel.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨רַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים עַל הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: David said to Divine, I have sinned greatly by doing this; now remove guilt of servant, for I acted very foolishly.

familiar.text: And David said unto God, I have sinned greatly, because I have done this thing: but now, I beseech thee, do away the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.

modern.text: Then David said to God, “I have sinned greatly because I have done this thing. Now I beg You to take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Gad, David's seer, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Gad, David’s seer, saying,

modern.text: And the LORD instructed Gad, David’s seer,

verses.restored: Go and speak to David: Thus says YHWH, Three things I offer you; choose one, and I will do it to you.

familiar.text: Go and tell David, saying, Thus saith the LORD, I offer thee three things: choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.

modern.text: “Go and tell David that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’”

verses.restored: Gad came to David and said, Thus says YHWH, Choose for yourself:

familiar.text: So Gad came to David, and said unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Choose thee

modern.text: So Gad went and said to David, “This is what the LORD says: ‘You must choose

original.text: וַיָּ֥בֹא גָ֖ד אֶל דָּוִ֑יד וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֛וֹ כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה קַבֶּל לָֽךְ

verses.restored: three years of famine, three months swept away before foes while enemies' sword overtakes, or three days sword of YHWH—plague in land and messenger of YHWH destroying throughout Israel. Now consider what word I shall return.

familiar.text: Either three years’ famine; or three months to be destroyed before thy foes, while that the sword of thine enemies overtaketh thee; or else three days the sword of the LORD, even the pestilence, in the land, and the angel of the LORD destroying throughout all the coasts of Israel. Now therefore advise thyself what word I shall bring again to him that sent me.

modern.text: between three years of famine, three months of being swept away before your enemies and overtaken by their swords, or three days of the sword of the LORD—days of plague upon the land, with the angel of the LORD ravaging every part of Israel.’ Now then, decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”

verses.restored: David said to Gad, I am in great distress. Let me fall into hand of YHWH, for very great are mercies, but let me not fall into human hand.

familiar.text: And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let me fall now into the hand of the LORD; for very great are his mercies: but let me not fall into the hand of man.

modern.text: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.” A Plague on Israel (2 Samuel 24:15–17)

verses.restored: YHWH sent plague upon Israel, and seventy thousand people of Israel fell.

familiar.text: So the LORD sent pestilence upon Israel: and there fell of Israel seventy thousand men.

modern.text: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell dead.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה דֶּ֖בֶר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּפֹּל֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: Divine sent a messenger to Jerusalem to destroy it; as destruction occurred, YHWH saw and relented concerning harm and said to destroying messenger, Enough; now release your hand. Messenger of YHWH stood by threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

familiar.text: And God sent an angel unto Jerusalem to destroy it: and as he was destroying, the LORD beheld, and he repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed, It is enough, stay now thine hand. And the angel of the LORD stood by the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.

modern.text: Then God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem, but as the angel was doing so, the LORD saw it and relented from the calamity, and He said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הָאֱלֹהִ֨ים מַלְאָ֥ךְ לִֽירוּשָׁלִַם֮ לְהַשְׁחִיתָהּ֒ וּכְהַשְׁחִ֗ית רָאָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם עַל הָֽרָעָ֔ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לַמַּלְאָ֤ךְ הַמַּשְׁחִית֙ רַ֔ב עַתָּ֖ה הֶ֣רֶף יָדֶ֑ךָ וּמַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ עֹמֵ֔ד עִם גֹּ֖רֶן אָרְנָ֥ן הַיְבוּסִֽי

verses.restored: David lifted eyes and saw messenger of YHWH standing between earth and heavens, drawn sword in hand stretched over Jerusalem. David and elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell on faces.

familiar.text: And David lifted up his eyes, and saw the angel of the LORD stand between the earth and the heaven, having a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders of Israel, who were clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces.

modern.text: When David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem, David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell facedown.

original.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א דָוִ֜יד אֶת עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּ֞רְא אֶת מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ עֹמֵ֗ד בֵּ֤ין הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְחַרְבּ֤וֹ שְׁלוּפָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ נְטוּיָ֖ה עַל יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּפֹּ֨ל דָּוִ֧יד וְהַזְּקֵנִ֛ים מְכֻסִּ֥ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֖ים עַל פְּנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: David said to Divine, Was it not I who commanded people counted? I am one who sinned and did evil; these sheep, what have they done? YHWH my Divine, let your hand be against me and father's house, but not against your people as plague.

familiar.text: And David said unto God, Is it not I that commanded the people to be numbered? even I it is that have sinned and done evil indeed; but as for these sheep, what have they done? let thine hand, I pray thee, O LORD my God, be on me, and on my father’s house; but not on thy people, that they should be plagued.

modern.text: And David said to God, “Was it not I who gave the order to count the people? I am the one who has sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? O LORD my God, please let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house, but do not let this plague remain upon Your people.” David Builds an Altar (2 Samuel 24:18–25)

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH told Gad to say to David that David should go up and establish altar to YHWH at threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

familiar.text: Then the angel of the LORD commanded Gad to say to David, that David should go up, and set up an altar unto the LORD in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.

modern.text: Then the angel of the LORD ordered Gad to tell David to go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

original.text: וּמַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֶל גָּ֖ד לֵאמֹ֣ר לְדָוִ֑יד כִּ֣י יַעֲלֶ֣ה דָוִ֗יד לְהָקִ֤ים מִזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה בְּגֹ֖רֶן אָרְנָ֥ן הַיְבֻסִֽי

verses.restored: David went up according to word Gad spoke in name of YHWH.

familiar.text: And David went up at the saying of Gad, which he spake in the name of the LORD.

modern.text: So David went up at the word that Gad had spoken in the name of the LORD.

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַל דָּוִיד֙ בִּדְבַר גָּ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Ornan turned and saw messenger; his four sons with him hid themselves. Ornan was threshing wheat.

familiar.text: And Ornan turned back, and saw the angel; and his four sons with him hid themselves. Now Ornan was threshing wheat.

modern.text: Now Ornan was threshing wheat when he turned and saw the angel; and his four sons who were with him hid themselves.

original.text: וַיָּ֣שָׁב אָרְנָ֗ן וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת הַמַּלְאָ֔ךְ וְאַרְבַּ֧עַת בָּנָ֛יו עִמּ֖וֹ מִֽתְחַבְּאִ֑ים וְאָרְנָ֖ן דָּ֥שׁ חִטִּֽים

familiar.text: And as David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David, and went out of the threshingfloor, and bowed himself to David with his face to the ground.

modern.text: David came to Ornan, and when Ornan looked out and saw David, he left the threshing floor and bowed facedown before David.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א דָוִ֖יד עַד אָרְנָ֑ן וַיַּבֵּ֤ט אָרְנָן֙ וַיַּ֣רְא אֶת דָּוִ֔יד וַיֵּצֵא֙ מִן הַגֹּ֔רֶן וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ לְדָוִ֛יד אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה

verses.restored: David said to Ornan, Give me site of threshing floor, that I may build altar to YHWH; for full price give it to me, so plague may be restrained from people.

familiar.text: Then David said to Ornan, Grant me the place of this threshingfloor, that I may build an altar therein unto the LORD: thou shalt grant it me for the full price: that the plague may be stayed from the people.

modern.text: Then David said to Ornan, “Grant me the site of this threshing floor, that I may build an altar to the LORD. Sell it to me for the full price, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד אֶל אָרְנָ֗ן תְּנָה לִּי֙ מְק֣וֹם הַגֹּ֔רֶן וְאֶבְנֶה בּ֥וֹ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַיהוָ֑ה בְּכֶ֤סֶף מָלֵא֙ תְּנֵ֣הוּ לִ֔י וְתֵעָצַ֥ר הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל הָעָֽם

verses.restored: Ornan said to David, Take it; let my lord king do what is good in his eyes. See, I give oxen for burnt offerings, threshing sledges for wood, and wheat for grain offering; I give all.

familiar.text: And Ornan said unto David, Take it to thee, and let my lord the king do that which is good in his eyes: lo, I give thee the oxen also for burnt offerings, and the threshing instruments for wood, and the wheat for the meat offering; I give it all.

modern.text: Ornan said to David, “My lord the king may take whatever seems good. Look, I will give the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood, and the wheat for the grain offering—I will give it all.”

translation_notes: 2 Samuel 24:1 says YHWH incited David; 1 Chronicles 21:1 attributes incitement to an adversary/Satan. The contradiction must remain visible.
Counting people is not inherently sinful. Likely concerns include military conscription, taxation, royal possession, or distrust, but the text does not fully explain.
Joab's resistance is overridden by royal command, showing that a subordinate's ethical objection can be valid even when the objector is morally compromised elsewhere.
Famine, military defeat, and plague fall chiefly on ordinary people rather than the king who chose the census. Collective punishment is not justice.
Seventy thousand deaths may not become props for David's lesson or evidence that epidemics punish sin.
The clearest ethical command is 'Enough; release your hand.' Mercy interrupts destruction rather than glorifying it.
David calls people sheep; his admission of responsibility is important, but people are not royal property or passive livestock.
Ornan is a Jebusite landowner approached by a king during catastrophe. Bowing and offering everything do not prove free consent under extreme power imbalance.
Ornan's four sons hide from the angelic threat; child/family terror remains part of the site-acquisition story.
The price differs sharply from 2 Samuel 24:24; numbers, site scope, agency, and plague details require textual audit.
Fire from heaven and angelic imagery are not instructions for ritual technique, plague control, or violence.
safety_note: Reject epidemic-punishment theology, collective punishment, census superstition, coerced land transfer, angelic-war imitation, and leader-centered grief. Center the seventy thousand dead, terrified families, Joab's refusal, David's responsibility, Ornan's ownership, and the command: Enough—release your hand.
